about: Every value in this file was entered from a source actually consulted during the Milestone 8 build session (2026-11-06) and is cited per entry, or is explicitly status-flagged. Status meanings: 'cited' = value taken from the cited source; 'calibrated' = value chosen by the build within a cited published range, choice disclosed in the note and in MILESTONE-8.md; 'verify' = engineering placeholder with NO literature source — never to be read as a physiological value. Units are carried on every entry. Milestone 18 additions (sources S13-S16, the venomotor and transcapillary-refill parameters, the widened heart-rate multiplier bound, and the magnitude-gated perturbation expectations) were likewise entered from sources consulted during the Milestone 18 session (2026-11-06) and are cited per entry; amendments to Milestone 8 entries are appended to those entries' notes, never silently rewritten. Milestone 21 additions (the contractility/inotropy effector parameters, transcribed from the S13 supplement re-read during the Milestone 21 session, 2026-11-06) follow the same rule. Milestone 24 additions (sources S17-S22, the right-atrial-pressure validation range, the haemorrhage-course case, and an appended amendment on the haemorrhage_1500 heart-rate expectation) were likewise entered from sources consulted during the Milestone 24 session (2026-11-06); Milestone 24 adds NO model parameter — the Guyton quantities it reports are computed functions of the existing state. Milestone 25 additions (sources S23-S28, the interstitial reservoir parameters, the lumped renal function curve parameters, the urine-output validation range, the bolus-retention course expectation, and appended amendments on refill_reserve_ml, refill_conductance_ml_s_mmhg, the course case and the refill observation) were likewise entered from sources consulted during the Milestone 25 session (2026-11-06) and are cited per entry.

parameters.name: tick_seconds
parameters.note: Interface/event timestep per design/04 (Pulse's published step). The integrator substeps inside each tick (see substep_seconds).

parameters.name: substep_seconds
parameters.note: Numerical integration substep (40 per tick), RK4. Engineering choice for stability against the stiffest model time constants (arterial compliance x arterial resistance ~17 ms); not a physiological value. VERIFY-flagged as an unsourced numerical parameter.

parameters.name: heart_rate_baseline_bpm
parameters.note: S1 protocol: 'in all simulations the heart rate was set at 60 beats per minute' with a 1 s cycle. The resting normal range 60-100 bpm is S11; 60 sits at its lower bound.

parameters.name: ventricular_systole_seconds_at_1s_cycle
parameters.note: S1: ventricular activation v(t) = sin^2(pi * tR / tv) for tR in [0, tv], tv = 0.45 s 'defining duration of ventricular systole including periods of isovolumic contraction and relaxation', at a 1 s cycle.

parameters.name: systole_duration_hr_exponent
parameters.note: tv scaling when the baroreflex changes heart rate: tv = 0.45 * sqrt(cycle_seconds / 1 s). S1 fixes HR at 60 bpm and gives no scaling law; this square-root scaling is an engineering placeholder. VERIFY before any use where systole duration at non-60 bpm rates matters.

parameters.name: total_blood_volume_ml
parameters.note: Cited range: 4,900 mL = 70 mL/kg x 70 kg (S8) to 5,570 mL = the S1 model baseline. CALIBRATED VALUE 5,000 mL — S8 textbook value for the 70-kg reference adult (about 5 L). Calibration sweep (MILESTONE-8.md section 3): at 5,570 mL every pressure output overshoots its published range in this reduced compartment set (v0 omits S1 atrial chambers and pericardium, whose compliance holds volume at low pressure in S1 model); at 4,900 mL MAP and CO undershoot. 5,000 mL is the value at which the resting case meets every gated published range.

parameters.name: blood_density_kg_m3
parameters.note: Used only in the Bernoulli valve law. S9 physiological range 1052-1062; S12 reports literature values 1043-1060. 1060 lies in both consulted ranges.

parameters.name: valve_area_av_cm2
parameters.note: Effective orifice area, atrioventricular valves (mitral, tricuspid): 'effective orifice areas for atrioventricular valves were set to 7 cm2' (S1).

parameters.name: valve_area_semilunar_cm2
parameters.note: Effective orifice area, aortic and pulmonary valves: 'aortic and pulmonary valve areas were set to 5 cm2' (S1). S1 also sets valve length L = 1 cm for the inertance term; inertance is omitted in v0 (documented simplification), so L is recorded here as cited-but-unused.

parameters.name: valve_regularization_r
parameters.note: Small linear term added to the Bernoulli valve law (deltaP = B*Q^2 + r*Q) purely to keep dQ/d(deltaP) finite at valve opening. Numerical regularization, NOT a physiological valve resistance. VERIFY-flagged.

parameters.name: reflex_tau_seconds
parameters.note: Baroreflex sensing lag: first-order low-pass time constant on measured MAP. Engineering placeholder, no literature source consulted. VERIFY.

parameters.name: reflex_gain_hr
parameters.note: Baroreflex heart-rate gain: hr_multiplier = clamp(1 + gain * (setpoint - MAP_lp)/setpoint). Engineering placeholder chosen for bounded, non-oscillatory response; NOT a measured physiological gain. VERIFY before any interpretive use. MILESTONE 18 AMENDMENT: value raised 4.0 -> 12.0. The gain remains an unsourced engineering placeholder (VERIFY); 12.0 is the value at which, with the sourced venomotor mechanism (S13) active, the model's heart-rate response to a 750 mL haemorrhage lands inside the published ATLS Class II band (100-120 /min, S16) — a calibration of a placeholder to a published presentation band, disclosed as such and reported with the sweep in MILESTONE-18.md. It is not a measured baroreflex gain.

parameters.name: reflex_gain_resistance
parameters.note: Baroreflex peripheral-resistance gain on r_systemic_capillaries, same error signal as reflex_gain_hr. Engineering placeholder. VERIFY.

parameters.name: reflex_hr_mult_bounds
parameters.note: Saturation bounds for the heart-rate multiplier. Engineering placeholder. VERIFY. MILESTONE 18 AMENDMENT: upper bound raised 1.9 -> 2.4 so this placeholder cannot clip the published ATLS pulse range — at the 60 bpm baseline a 1.9 bound caps heart rate at 114/min, below the Class III (120-140) and Class IV (>140) bands consulted at S16. Still an engineering placeholder, not a measured physiological limit. VERIFY.

parameters.name: reflex_r_mult_bounds
parameters.note: Saturation bounds for the resistance multiplier. Engineering placeholder. VERIFY.

parameters.name: venomotor_capacity_ml
parameters.note: Baroreflex venomotor recruitment capacity: the maximal sympathetic swing of venous unstressed volume in the published Ursino-lineage baroreflex model (S13). Steady state Vun = gamma + alpha*ns = 3630 - 1260*ns mL with resting ns = 0.5 (Vun,0 = 3000 mL, S13 Tables S1/S7); maximal sympathetic drive (ns -> 1) gives Vun = 2370 mL — 630 mL of unstressed volume shifted into stressed volume — and ns -> 0 gives the symmetric +630 mL dilation. This engine adopts the 630 mL swing magnitude around its own S1 venous unstressed volume (2747 mL); it does not adopt S13's absolute volumes, sigmoid, or sympathetic-activity state.

parameters.name: venomotor_tau_seconds
parameters.note: First-order time constant of the venous unstressed-volume effector in S13's baroreflex equations (tau_v = 60 s, Table S7; the arterial-resistance effector there is 12 s, the heart effector 3 s). Venomotor recruitment is therefore the slow baroreflex limb: ~63% of target at 60 s, ~95% at 180 s.

parameters.name: venomotor_gain
parameters.note: Proportional gain mapping the baroreflex MAP error signal (the same normalised error the HR and resistance effectors use) to the recruited fraction of venomotor_capacity_ml: target = capacity * clamp(gain * err, -1, 1). Engineering placeholder of the same class as reflex_gain_hr / reflex_gain_resistance, chosen for a bounded, non-oscillatory response; NO literature source. The cited quantities are the capacity and time constant (S13); this gain is not a physiological claim. VERIFY. Value 12.0 was exercised in the Milestone 18 calibration sweep (venomotor gain x heart-rate gain grid, MILESTONE-18.md): at 12.0 the -750 mL case simultaneously satisfies the hard ATLS Class II heart-rate gate and the S15 refill band with resting MAP and cardiac output unmoved to two decimals (73.09->73.08 mmHg, 4.21->4.21 L/min; resting heart rate and stroke volume move within their cited ranges, see MILESTONE-18.md).

parameters.name: contractility_tau_seconds
parameters.note: First-order time constant of the ventricular-elastance (inotropy) effector in S13's baroreceptor equations (S25): dE_lv,max/dt = (-E_lv,max + alpha_Elv * ns + gamma_Elv) / tau_h, with tau_h = 3 s (Table S7; the arterial-resistance effector there is 12 s, the venous 60 s). Contractility is the fast sympathetic limb, acting on the heart effector's own cited time constant — distinct from this engine's verify-flagged reflex sensing lag (reflex_tau_seconds), which it happens to share numerically.

parameters.name: contractility_swing_fraction
parameters.note: Maximal sympathetic swing of maximal ventricular elastance, as a fraction of the resting value, from S13's elastance effector (S25 with Tables S1/S7). LV steady-state target E = alpha_Elv * ns + gamma_Elv = 1.0 * ns + 2.0 mmHg/mL passes through the resting Elv,max,0 = 2.5 mmHg/mL (Table S1) at the resting sympathetic activity ns = 0.5 (S28), and reaches 3.0 mmHg/mL at ns = 1 and 2.0 mmHg/mL at ns = 0: a +/-20% swing. RV: 0.46 * ns + 0.92 about Erv,max,0 = 1.15 mmHg/mL is the identical +/-20% fraction, so one shared multiplier state modulates both ventricles. This engine adopts the swing fraction and the time constant; it does not adopt S13's absolute elastances (its own are S1's: LV 2.8, RV 0.8 mmHg/mL), its sigmoid, or its sympathetic-activity state — the same adoption discipline as the venomotor capacity at Milestone 18.

parameters.name: contractility_gain
parameters.note: Proportional gain mapping the baroreflex MAP error signal (the same normalised error the HR, resistance and venomotor effectors use) to the driven fraction of contractility_swing_fraction: multiplier target = 1 + swing * clamp(gain * err, -1, 1), approached first-order at contractility_tau_seconds. Engineering placeholder of the same class as venomotor_gain; NO literature source. The cited quantities are the swing fraction and time constant (S13); this gain is not a physiological claim. VERIFY. MILESTONE 21 SWEEP: with all other parameters at their Milestone 18 values, gains {4, 8, 12, 20} were exercised; every hard gate passes at every cell and the response surface is shallow (post-haemorrhage heart rate at -750 mL spans 103.2 -> 101.0 /min across the grid, refill at +30 min 191.6 -> 184.6 mL in band, -1,500 mL MAP 29.8 -> 29.6 mmHg — the Class III picture is preload-bound, not gain-bound). Shipped value 12.0 by parity with the sibling effector gains set at Milestone 18 (reflex_gain_hr 12.0, venomotor_gain 12.0); the choice is a disclosed convention, not an identification.

parameters.name: refill_conductance_ml_s_mmhg
parameters.note: Net transcapillary refill conductance in Q_refill = k * (Pcap_ref - Pcap_lp), the lumped Starling form: refill is driven by the fall of mean systemic capillary pressure below its own resting value. CALIBRATED within a band derived from consulted human data: S15's volunteer trajectory (~25% of a moderate loss restored in 30 min; up to 25-50% in the first hour) and S14's measured capability (net absorption up to 0.147 mL/min per 100 mL soft tissue under strong LBNP; authors' whole-body estimate up to ~600 mL in 10 min). Identification is trajectory-level: in this model the driving deficit measures only ~3.6 mmHg at the end of a 750 mL bleed (the lumped capillary segment's pressure is flow-dominated: ~63 mmHg at rest, ~59 mmHg at bleed end — both measured in the Milestone 18 build), so this conductance is a NET whole-body lumped coefficient against that lumped signal, NOT a single-capillary filtration coefficient. Across k in [0.008, 0.08] the 30-minute observation refill spans roughly 35-290 mL; the chosen 0.04 lands it at 194 mL = 25.9% of the 750 mL loss, on S15's cited ~25% point (sweeps in MILESTONE-18.md). MILESTONE 25 AMENDMENT: the driver gains the interstitial pressure feedback term — Q_refill = k * [ (Pcap_ref - Pcap_lp) - refill_ml / interstitial_compliance_ml_mmhg ] — now that the interstitium is a finite reservoir with a pressure (Milestone 25). The conductance k itself is unchanged and was NOT re-tuned to compensate: the feedback only brakes flows the Milestone 18 calibration produced, and the 30-minute observation remains inside its cited band under the braked dynamics (measured values in MILESTONE-25.md).

parameters.name: refill_reserve_ml
parameters.note: Total interstitial fluid recruitable by transcapillary refill in one episode (the refill state's upper bound; the interstitium itself is not a compartment in this engine). S15: refill 'can restore plasma volume by 500-1000 mL within 1-2 hours'. Upper end of the cited range taken; the choice is non-binding in every shipped scenario (largest modelled refill is ~200 mL in the 30-minute observation) and binds only in multi-hour or repeated-loss runs. The same bound caps net transcapillary escape in the infusion direction — a symmetric lumped bound, disclosed as a modelling bound rather than a measured interstitial capacity. MILESTONE 25 AMENDMENT: this parameter is NO LONGER the refill flow's bound. Milestone 25 gives the interstitium a finite volume (interstitial_volume_ml) and a pressure (interstitial_compliance_ml_mmhg): the flow is now limited by the reservoir's physical floor (no refill once the interstitial volume would go negative) and braked continuously by the interstitial pressure feedback. The parameter is retained because S15's 500-1000 mL figure remains the cited envelope the 60-minute course refill trajectory is read against (the course's soft refill line), and the value still appears in that comparison; it no longer constrains any flow.

parameters.name: interstitial_volume_ml
parameters.note: Milestone 25: the finite capacity of the interstitial reservoir the transcapillary refill state draws on and the infusion escape drains into. The interstitial volume is tracked by identity, not integrated as a separate state: V_isf = interstitial_volume_ml - refill_ml at all times (the refill state IS the net transfer integral, as since Milestone 18). Value 11,000 mL inside the cited band: S25 gives the extracellular fluid as typically 15 L of which 12 L is interstitial fluid, and separately 'about 11 liters' of interstitial fluid on average; the classical 70-kg accounting in the same tradition (ECF ~14 L, plasma ~3 L) puts the interstitium near 10-11 L. Before Milestone 25 the interstitium had no volume in this engine at all — refill was bounded only by refill_reserve_ml.

parameters.name: interstitial_compliance_ml_mmhg
parameters.note: Milestone 25: the single lumped linear compliance of the interstitial reservoir, entering the Starling driver as a pressure feedback: Q_refill = k * [ (Pcap_ref - Pcap_lp) - refill_ml / C_isf ], i.e. the interstitial pressure deviation from its operating point is dP_isf = -refill_ml / C_isf (depleting the interstitium lowers its pressure and brakes further refill; filling it raises its pressure and brakes further escape). CALIBRATED inside a band derived from S26's fitted experimental pressure-volume relation: that fit's local slope at the operating point is ~30 mmHg per unit fractional volume change, falling to ~20 and rising to ~55 mmHg across the volume range the shipped scenarios visit (x = V/V0 in 0.92-1.05), which scaled to an 11,000 mL interstitium is roughly 200-550 mL/mmHg; the band's lower edge adds margin for deeper depletion. DISCLOSED SIMPLIFICATION: the source curve is strongly nonlinear (very steep in the negative-pressure region, then near-ballooning above zero pressure — the edema regime); a single slope cannot reproduce both regimes. The shipped scenarios move the interstitial volume by at most a few hundred mL (a few percent of V0), inside the region the band was derived from; sustained-edema behaviour is out of scope and would need the nonlinear curve. MILESTONE 25 SWEEP: C_isf in {200, 300, 400} mL/mmHg was exercised against the full gate set — 30-minute observation refill 158.9 / 167.6 / 172.2 mL (band 112.5-262.5), 60-minute course refill (untreated) 615.8 / 682.4 / 720.1 mL (soft envelope 500-1000), bolus retention at +60 min 0.54 / 0.49 / 0.46 (soft band 0.20-0.95), resting outputs identical at recorded precision — every hard gate and every soft line holds at all three cells and the surface is shallow and monotone. Shipped value 300: the middle of the fit-implied range over the visited volume band (the fit's slope implies ~235-370 mL/mmHg for x in 0.94-1.0); the choice within the sweep is a disclosed convention, not an identification.

parameters.name: baseline_urine_output_ml_min
parameters.note: Milestone 25: U0, the urine output of the lumped renal function curve at the model's operating point (the value the curve takes where arterial pressure equals the captured setpoint). 1.0 mL/min = 1,440 mL/day, inside S24's cited normal production of 1-2 litres of urine per day (0.69-1.39 mL/min); S24's worked table value is 0.9 mL/min (1,296 mL/day). This is a lumped Guyton-tradition renal function curve, NOT nephron modelling: the Body Model has no nephron either (Milestones 12/23: the urinary interior is absent from the source anatomies), and the engine represents the kidney only through this pressure-output relation.

parameters.name: fluid_intake_ml_min
parameters.note: Milestone 25: constant lumped fluid intake (drinking + food water, entering the systemic venous compartment), set EQUAL to baseline_urine_output_ml_min by Guyton's equilibrium construction (S23): the equilibrium point of the renal-body fluid system is where the intake line intersects the renal output curve, so a model that sits at its operating point must take in what it excretes there. The source figure's own note applies: nonrenal losses are ignored in that construction, and they are ignored here too (no insensible-loss term). During the reflex-off settle, urine output is held exactly equal to intake so the settle is undisturbed; once the reflexes engage, the renal curve acts on the sensed MAP and the two fluxes separate.

parameters.name: renal_pressure_zero_offset_mmhg
parameters.note: Milestone 25: in S23's renal urinary output curve (Figure 19-1), urine output is essentially zero at an arterial pressure 50 mmHg below the normal pressure (zero at 50 mmHg, normal at 100 mmHg). CITED as the curve's zero anchor. The curve's SHAPE is applied relative to this model's captured operating point (the setpoint captured at reflex engagement) — the engine's standing self-referencing convention, used for the baroreflex setpoint since v0 and for the refill capillary reference since Milestone 18 — because the model's operating MAP (~73 mmHg, set by the lumped S1 vascular parameters) sits below the source's 100 mmHg normal; what is cited and carried is the shape (offsets and multiples), not the source's absolute pressure axis.

parameters.name: renal_multiple_at_plus_50_mmhg
parameters.note: Milestone 25: S23's Figure 19-3 analysis — at an arterial pressure 50 mmHg above the normal pressure (150 vs 100 mmHg), 'renal output of water and salt is about three times as great as the intake'. CITED as the curve's midpoint anchor: urine output = 3 x U0 at +50 mmHg relative to the operating point.

parameters.name: renal_multiple_at_plus_100_mmhg
parameters.note: Milestone 25: S23's Figure 19-1 text — at an arterial pressure 100 mmHg above the normal pressure (200 vs 100 mmHg), urine output rises 'to about six to eight times normal'. CITED as the curve's upper anchor at the band midpoint, 7 x U0; above +100 mmHg the curve continues at the [50, 100] segment's slope (0.08 x U0 per mmHg), disclosed as extrapolation beyond the cited anchors. The shipped curve is the chapter's ACUTE (isolated-kidney) shape; the chronic in-vivo curve is far steeper, partly through sympathetic and hormonal mechanisms this engine does not model (S23) — named in the Milestone 25 caveat ledger.

parameters.name: steady_state_drift_tolerance
parameters.note: Harness criterion: |second-half mean - first-half mean| / mean < 1% for MAP and CO across the measurement window counts as 'holding steady state'. An engineering acceptance threshold for the design/04 'holds published normal ranges indefinitely' gate, not a physiological value. VERIFY-flagged as a chosen criterion.

parameters.name: plasma_protein_concentration_g_ml
parameters.note: Milestone 26: resting plasma total protein concentration, S29's table (albumin 4.5 + globulins 2.5 + fibrinogen 0.3 = 7.3 g/dL). Initialises the lumped plasma protein mass state over the derived resting plasma volume (total blood volume x (1 - hematocrit_resting)); thereafter the concentration is a derived quantity of the protein mass and plasma volume states.

parameters.name: isf_protein_concentration_g_ml
parameters.note: Milestone 26: resting interstitial fluid protein concentration, S29 (interstitial protein averages about 3 g/dL, giving the interstitial oncotic pressure of 8 mmHg). Initialises the lumped interstitial protein mass state over the interstitial reservoir volume (Milestone 25); thereafter derived.

parameters.name: hematocrit_resting
parameters.note: Milestone 26: the model subject's resting hematocrit. S35's whole-blood unit band is 0.35-0.45 and S34's per-unit rule assumes the standard adult; 0.45 is taken inside the cited span. The red-cell volume state is initialised as this fraction of total blood volume. TRACKED-BUT-INERT, stated plainly: hematocrit feeds only the plasma-volume identity (V_plasma = V_blood - V_rbc) and the product/dilution bookkeeping. No viscosity coupling is modelled - no sourced lumped viscosity law was consulted, and inventing one is refused (see MILESTONE-26.md).

parameters.name: starling_reflection_coefficient_protein
parameters.note: Milestone 26: osmotic reflection coefficient for total plasma protein, S30 (about 0.9 in muscle microvessels; tissue span roughly 0.7-0.99 quoted there). Enters the Starling driver as sigma x (oncotic pressure difference) and the convective protein flux on the filtration limb as the sieving factor (1 - sigma). A lumped whole-body value, dominated by muscle/skin beds; the fenestrated and discontinuous beds (liver, gut) have far lower sigma and are not distinguished in a lumped state - disclosed in MILESTONE-26.md.

parameters.name: oncotic_albumin_coefficients
parameters.note: Milestone 26: Nitta et al.'s albumin-fraction polynomial coefficients (linear, quadratic, cubic) of the corrected Landis-Pappenheimer relation, S33, concentrations in g/dL, result in mmHg.

parameters.name: oncotic_globulin_coefficients
parameters.note: Milestone 26: Nitta et al.'s non-albumin (globulin) fraction polynomial coefficients of the same relation, S33.

parameters.name: plasma_albumin_fraction
parameters.note: Milestone 26: albumin fraction of total plasma protein = 4.5 / 7.3 from S29's own table, held FIXED: the lumped states track total protein only, so the Nitta relation (S33) is applied at this resting composition in both pools. S33's exchange notes the albumin fraction is one source of the 10-15% inter-equation spread; the interstitial pool's true albumin fraction differs from plasma's and is not distinguished - disclosed in MILESTONE-26.md.

parameters.name: lymph_protein_return_g_s
parameters.note: Milestone 26: resting lymphatic protein return flux L0 = 70 g/day, calibrated inside S32's cited band (protein returned via lymph in one day = 25-50% of the circulating pool; this model's pool is about 201 g, so the band is 50-100 g/day = [5.79e-4, 1.157e-3] g/s; the 3 L/day lymph flow at interstitial concentration cross-checks at 60-90 g/day). In-model the return scales with the interstitial concentration ratio (ci/ci0) and the balancing transcapillary leak with the plasma concentration ratio (cp/cp0), so both fluxes follow dilution and concentration honestly and are exactly equal at the operating point.

parameters.name: albumin_synthesis_g_s
parameters.note: Milestone 26: albumin synthesis 10.5 g/day (S31) = 1.2153e-4 g/s, applied to the lumped total-protein plasma pool. Albumin is only about 60% of plasma protein mass, so applying the albumin rate to the total pool UNDERSTATES total-protein synthesis: oncotic recovery in-model is slower than a full total-protein synthesis would produce, never faster. A disclosed conservative choice - the alternative (scaling up by an assumed albumin share) would invent a number.

parameters.name: protein_catabolic_fraction_s
parameters.note: Milestone 26: first-order fractional clearance of the plasma protein pool, DERIVED so that synthesis and catabolism cancel exactly at the resting operating point: kappa = synthesis rate (S31, 1.2153e-4 g/s) / resting circulating pool (200.75 g: S29 concentration over the derived 2,750 mL plasma volume) = 6.05e-7 /s. Quiet-at-rest by construction, the same equilibrium device as intake = U0 (Milestone 25). The cited band spans synthesis 9-14 g/day over pools of 150-250 g. S31's clearance split (renal ~6%, gastrointestinal ~10%, catabolic ~84%) is represented by this single lumped sink; the kidney's protein handling is NOT a urine-protein model and no protein appears in the urine state.

parameters.name: product_whole_blood_volume_ml
parameters.note: Milestone 26: one unit of whole blood = 450 mL donor blood + 63 mL anticoagulant-preservative (S35). Scenario inputs are whole units; the course whole-blood arm gives 2 units = 1,026 mL, volume-matched by design to the 1,000 mL crystalloid bolus arm within the units' quantisation (disclosed in MILESTONE-26.md).

parameters.name: product_whole_blood_hematocrit
parameters.note: Milestone 26: hematocrit of a whole-blood unit, S35's band 0.35-0.45; mid-band value taken.

parameters.name: product_whole_blood_protein_g_ml
parameters.note: Milestone 26: DERIVED: the unit's plasma fraction at its hematocrit (1 - 0.40) x the plasma protein concentration (S29, 0.073 g/mL) = 0.0438 g/mL. The 63 mL of anticoagulant dilutes the unit by about 12% and that dilution is neglected, which slightly OVERSTATES the unit's protein - disclosed; the term is small against the course effects reported.

parameters.name: product_prbc_volume_ml
parameters.note: Milestone 26: one unit of packed red blood cells. S34's institutional table lists 350 mL; S35's component references give 250-320 mL; 300 mL sits inside both.

parameters.name: product_prbc_hematocrit
parameters.note: Milestone 26: hematocrit of a packed red cell unit, S35's band 0.50-0.70 (additive-solution units 0.55-0.65); 0.60 taken.

parameters.name: product_prbc_protein_g_ml
parameters.note: Milestone 26: DERIVED residual-plasma estimate: (1 - 0.60) x 0.073 g/mL (S29). Additive-solution units carry crystalloid in place of part of that residual plasma, so this overstates PRBC protein somewhat - disclosed. The term exists so the protein bookkeeping is complete for every product; PRBC is not administered for its protein in any scenario here.

parameters.name: product_plasma_volume_ml
parameters.note: Milestone 26: one unit of plasma (fresh frozen plasma class), S34's band 200-250 mL; mid-band value taken.

parameters.name: product_plasma_hematocrit
parameters.note: Milestone 26: plasma is an acellular component (S35) - it carries no red-cell volume.

parameters.name: product_plasma_protein_g_ml
parameters.note: Milestone 26: plasma product protein concentration = the plasma concentration (S29): FFP is separated plasma, so the donor plasma's protein concentration applies. Clotting-factor activity is not a state in this engine and is not claimed.

parameters.name: plasma_sodium_resting_mmol_l
parameters.note: Milestone 30: the equilibrium-construction concentration of the extracellular sodium lump, in the Milestone 25 intake-construction pattern: the sodium state is INITIALISED at this concentration over the extracellular volume (plasma + interstitial), so the resting operating point sits on it by construction - disclosed, not derived. S48 gives plasma sodium 137-144 mmol/L; the S46 teaching corpus gives about 140-145; the calibrated band spans both consulted ranges. Every flux then moves the state off this value only as the cited physiology dictates.

parameters.name: osmolality_non_sodium_mosm_kg
parameters.note: Milestone 30: the non-sodium terms of the calculated-osmolality formula (S47: 2[Na] + glucose/18 + BUN/2.8) at typical values - the consulted worked example (Na 140 mmol/L, glucose 90 mg/dL, BUN 14 mg/dL) gives 5 + 5 = 10 mOsm/kg and a total calculated osmolality of 290. Glucose and urea are not states in this engine; the term is carried as a constant and disclosed - the osmolality state's dynamics are sodium's. Resting calculated osmolality is therefore 2 x 138 + 10 = 286 mOsm/kg, inside the S47 band 275-295.

parameters.name: icf_volume_ml
parameters.note: Milestone 30: the intracellular water lump at rest. S46's consulted corpus puts intracellular water at about two thirds of total body water, 25-28 L at 70 kg; the upper end is taken so the model's summed body water (28,000 intracellular + 11,000 interstitial + 2,750 plasma = 41,750 mL) sits at the corpus's about-42 L total. The lump exchanges water with the interstitial compartment across the cell membrane on osmolality only; its solute content is fixed at the resting osmolality, so it is an osmotic buffer, not a sodium store - intracellular sodium/potassium exchange is not modelled (see MILESTONE-30.md).

parameters.name: icf_exchange_conductance_ml_s_mosm
parameters.note: Milestone 30: conductance of the intracellular-extracellular water exchange, per mOsm/kg of osmolality difference across the cell membrane. CALIBRATED construction, disclosed: the linearised equilibration time constant of the two-compartment system (28 L against 13.75 L) at this value is about 20 minutes; the cited band spans about 10-40 minutes. S36 establishes that body water distributes across the compartments on osmolality; no consulted source states a compartmental time constant directly - in vivo the appearance of an ingested load is absorption-limited (S40: water diuresis begins about 15 min after ingestion, maximum about 40 min). The span is an engineering bound around that physiology and is flagged as such.

parameters.name: adh_osmotic_threshold_mosm_kg
parameters.note: Milestone 30: threshold (x-intercept) of the plasma AVP-osmolality relation. S37 (primary human data, Robertson & Athar 1976): AVP = 0.35 x (osmolality - 281.0) in recumbent hydropenic subjects. S38's textbook threshold is 283 mOsm/kg and S36's about 280; the primary source's intercept is taken.

parameters.name: adh_osmotic_slope_pg_ml_per_mosm
parameters.note: Milestone 30: slope of the AVP-osmolality relation, S37: 0.35 pg/mL per mOsm/kg (recumbent hydropenic adults); the same study's upright (0.31) and hypertonic-saline (0.32) slopes bracket it from below. At the constructed resting osmolality 286 the relation gives a resting AVP of 0.35 x 5 = 1.75 pg/mL.

parameters.name: adh_volume_threshold_fraction
parameters.note: Milestone 30: the fall in intravascular volume / effective arterial pressure at which the non-osmotic (volume) stimulus to AVP secretion engages. S38: a decrease of 8 percent or more in intravascular volume or blood pressure triggers AVP release; S36 puts the required fall at 5-10 percent for effects comparable to osmotic stimuli (dual-sourced threshold). In this engine the sensed variable is the low-passed MAP deficit against the reflex set-point - the same sensed pressure the renal curve reads.

parameters.name: adh_volume_full_fraction
parameters.note: Milestone 30: the pressure/volume deficit at which the non-osmotic AVP stimulus reaches its cited full scale: S38 - at a 25 percent decrease in intravascular volume, AVP levels reach 20-30 times normal (the vasoconstrictor range).

parameters.name: adh_volume_max_pg_ml
parameters.note: Milestone 30: full-scale non-osmotic AVP contribution. S38's 20-30x normal at a 25 percent deficit, applied to this model's resting AVP (1.75 pg/mL, derived from S37 at the constructed resting osmolality), gives 35-53 pg/mL; 50 is taken inside that band. The volume limb adds to the osmotic limb, as in the cited physiology. AVP's own vasoconstrictor (V1) action at these levels is NOT an effector in this engine - disclosed in MILESTONE-30.md.

parameters.name: adh_tau_seconds
parameters.note: Milestone 30: lumped secretion-clearance time constant of the plasma AVP state. Dual-sourced span: S38 gives the plasma AVP half-life as 5-10 min; S36 gives 18 min. The value taken (1,080 s = 18 min) is the slow end, as a lumped approach constant for the secretion-plus-clearance limb; the cited band spans the two sources' half-lives converted to approach constants (about 5-26 min). The axis is fast next to aldosterone's hours - that ordering is the cited physiology, not a modelling choice.

parameters.name: adh_uosm_min_mosm_kg
parameters.note: Milestone 30: urine osmolality at maximal water diuresis (AVP absent), S39: the kidney can dilute urine to about 50 mOsm/kg in excess water.

parameters.name: adh_uosm_max_mosm_kg
parameters.note: Milestone 30: urine osmolality at maximal antidiuresis, S39: 1,200-1,400 mOsm/kg in water deficit; the lower end is taken (the human concentrating ceiling in most consulted accounts).

parameters.name: adh_uosm_half_pg_ml
parameters.note: Milestone 30: the AVP concentration at which the AVP-to-urine-osmolality response sits halfway between its cited floor (50, S39) and ceiling (1,200, S39). CALIBRATED to two cited anchors: S39's resting urine osmolarity of about 600 mOsm/kg at this model's resting AVP of 1.75 pg/mL (the response curve passes through 600 there at this value), and the cited near-maximal antidiuresis by 5-6 pg/mL (S38: maximal antidiuresis at about 5 pg/mL; S49: above 5-6 pg/mL urine osmolality is maximal) - at 5 pg/mL this curve reads about 1,065 mOsm/kg, 89 percent of ceiling. The response shape is a saturating Hill function with exponent 2; the exponent is an engineering choice, disclosed. This curve is what converts AVP into urine flow: flow = (the acute renal curve's pressure multiple) x (the urinary osmole excretion rate) / curve(AVP), so at the resting osmole rate the AVP term is exactly the ratio of the curve at the resting AVP to the curve at the current AVP, and the flow is exactly the baseline output at the operating point by construction. Formulating the flow on the osmole rate rather than on the baseline output alone is what keeps the urine-osmolality readout inside this curve's ceiling when the solute load itself moves (measured in MILESTONE-30.md).

parameters.name: baseline_sodium_excretion_mmol_min
parameters.note: Milestone 30: baseline renal sodium excretion at the resting operating point = 160 mmol/day. S45: on a normal diet sodium intake is 130-260 mmol/day (8-15 g NaCl), nearly completely absorbed, and at balance excretion matches intake; the population mean 24-h urinary sodium consulted alongside is 159 mmol/day. Sodium excretion is the output of the aldosterone-modulated CHRONIC renal curve (see renal_chronic_steepening and renal_curve_shift_per_aldosterone_mmhg); water excretion deliberately stays on the Milestone 25 acute curve.

parameters.name: sodium_intake_mmol_min
parameters.note: Milestone 30: baseline sodium intake, set EQUAL to baseline excretion by the equilibrium construction (the Milestone 25 fluid-intake pattern, disclosed): the resting sodium state is stationary because intake and excretion match at the operating point, not because either was derived. S45's normal-diet band applies. Scenario arms move this rate through the intake event; the theatre scenarios never do.

parameters.name: urine_non_sodium_osmole_rate_mosm_min
parameters.note: Milestone 30: DERIVED: the non-sodium urinary osmole excretion rate (urea-dominated), calibrated so the urine-osmolality readout reproduces S39's resting value: at the resting urine flow of 1.0 mL/min and resting sodium excretion of 0.111 mmol/min (2 x 0.111 = 0.222 mOsm/min of sodium salts), a resting urine osmolality of 600 mOsm/kg requires 0.600 - 0.222 = 0.378 mOsm/min of other osmoles; total solute excretion is then 0.600 mOsm/min = 864 mOsm/day. S39's mechanism - ADH changes water excretion at nearly constant solute excretion - is what makes the readout honest: the osmole rate is held constant and urine osmolality moves with the flow. The band spans plausible solute loads around the derivation.

parameters.name: crystalloid_sodium_mmol_l
parameters.note: Milestone 30: sodium concentration carried by the event channel's inflow ('isotonic crystalloid'). S50's consulted compositions: lactated Ringer 130 mmol/L, balanced solutions of the Plasma-Lyte class 140, 0.9% NaCl 154. The channel is a generic isotonic crystalloid, so the plasma-matched balanced value 140 is taken. Blood lost through the same channel removes sodium at the stage plasma concentration over the plasma (non-red-cell) fraction; administered blood products return sodium at the resting plasma concentration over their plasma fraction. Both conventions are disclosed in MILESTONE-30.md.

parameters.name: aldosterone_tau_seconds
parameters.note: Milestone 30: time constant of the aldosterone EFFECT state - not the hormone's plasma half-life, which S42 puts at about 20 min. The effect is genomic (transport proteins must be synthesised), so the span is set by S41's human infusion data (latent period about 20-60 min before a demonstrable effect on sodium excretion; peak effect 2-4 h; action lasting about 6 h) and S42 (transport changes begin after about 45 min and peak hours later) - dual-sourced. The value taken (7,200 s = 2 h) is the peak-effect midpoint. This is the slowest limb in the engine by design: the cited physiology is slow, and the model shows that timescale rather than making aldosterone a fast effector.

parameters.name: aldosterone_perfusion_gain
parameters.note: Milestone 30: VERIFY-FLAGGED engineering gain, in the house pattern of the baroreflex gains: the aldosterone effect state's target rises by this factor times the fractional MAP deficit against the reflex set-point (renal perfusion pressure is the RAAS input - S43's mechanism; renin and angiotensin II are subsumed into this limb rather than carried as states, disclosed in MILESTONE-30.md). Chosen with the sodium gain so the scenario arms behave in the cited regimes (sodium balance regained under a 5x load at a small pressure rise, S44's soft line; strong retention in haemorrhage). Nothing gates on this value alone; it awaits expert review like the reflex gains.

parameters.name: aldosterone_sodium_gain
parameters.note: Milestone 30: VERIFY-FLAGGED engineering gain: the aldosterone effect state's target falls by this factor times the fractional sodium-CONTENT excess over the resting content - the expansion limb of RAAS control (S43: suppression of the axis on high sodium intake is what makes pressure natriuresis effective at small pressure changes; S40: reduced salt intake raises aldosterone with slowly developing falls in sodium excretion). The input is the content error, not the concentration error, for a measured reason: water follows sodium, so under an isotonic load the plasma concentration error saturates below 1 percent while the content error reaches +21 percent - a concentration input cannot express the cited suppression (MILESTONE-30.md). The content error is the lump's expansion signal: the integrated renin pathway's inputs (renal perfusion, macula-densa delivery, atrial stretch) track the expanded state, not the clamped concentration. See aldosterone_perfusion_gain for the calibration disclosure.

parameters.name: aldosterone_target_floor
parameters.note: Milestone 30: engineering floor on the normalised aldosterone effect state (1.0 at rest), in the house pattern of the reflex bounds: maximal suppression keeps a residual sodium-retaining tone. VERIFY-FLAGGED; exercised by the scenario arms, nothing gates on the bound alone.

parameters.name: aldosterone_target_ceiling
parameters.note: Milestone 30: engineering ceiling on the normalised aldosterone effect state (1.0 at rest): caps the retaining state in deep volume deficit. VERIFY-FLAGGED; see aldosterone_target_floor.

parameters.name: renal_curve_shift_per_aldosterone_mmhg
parameters.note: Milestone 30: the aldosterone effect shifts the chronic pressure-natriuresis relation along the pressure axis by this many mmHg per unit of normalised aldosterone state - Guyton's formulation (S23: the hormonal state is among the determinants that shift the renal function curve; S43: suppression of the axis on high salt intake greatly amplifies the effectiveness of pressure natriuresis, and inappropriate activation forces pressure up to maintain sodium balance). CALIBRATED against the declared target - the 5x sodium-load arm regains sodium balance at a single-digit mmHg MAP rise, the regime S44 reports for intact-axis salt loading - and the calibration is a measurement, recorded here: at 12 mmHg per unit the arm ASYMPTOTES at 0.53 of balance (aldosterone state 0.48, MAP rise +2.2 mmHg at 24 h), because in this lump the Starling balance defends plasma volume and absorbs most of the pressure signal an expanded extracellular volume would otherwise send the kidney - the hormonal limb must therefore carry the natriuresis, which is S43's stated mechanism. At 25 the suppression carries it and balance closes at a small pressure rise (measured values in MILESTONE-30.md). The band runs from no shift to a shift comparable to the acute curve's own doubling offset (25 mmHg); the calibrated value sits at the band's top, disclosed.

parameters.name: renal_chronic_steepening
parameters.note: Milestone 30: the chronic renal curve for SODIUM reuses the Milestone 25 acute curve's shape with its pressure axis compressed by this factor. The compression is the cited physiology: S23 - the acute curve doubles output for about +25 mmHg, while chronically an increase in arterial pressure of only a few mmHg can double renal output, a steepening S23 attributes partly to the hormonal determinants (and S43 quantifies for the RAAS limb). Water excretion deliberately stays on the acute curve (the Milestone 25-validated behaviour); the asymmetry is named in MILESTONE-30.md - at sustained pressure elevation the model excretes sodium on the chronic relation but water on the acute one.

perturbation_cases.description: Acute hemorrhage of 750 mL, removed from the systemic venous compartment at a constant 12.5 mL/s over 60 s (lumped removal site = the venous reservoir; documented simplification). 750 mL is the ATLS Class I/II boundary for a 70-kg adult (S6, S7) and is 15.3% of the 4,900 mL weight-based blood volume (S8) — inside the 10-20% band within which S2 notes a person may remain asymptomatic, so expectations are directional only. MILESTONE 18: with venomotor recruitment and transcapillary refill modelled, two expectations are additionally magnitude-gated against the ATLS Class II bands (S16): heart rate 100-120 /min and systolic pressure inside the normal band. Directional expectations unchanged.

expectations.source: S2 ('as blood volume decreases, pressure and flow decrease'); S6/S7 (Class II: blood pressure normal-to-decreased, so a fall or near-hold is ATLS-consistent; the harness requires a fall because the model's reflex is deliberately partial — see MILESTONE-8.md) (No ATLS MAP band exists; MAP magnitude is reported, not gated.)

The numeric band is this file's resting systolic validation range (90-120 mmHg, S2-derived; its 90 mmHg lower bound is the conventional hypotension threshold and was flagged at Milestone 8 as not read in a consulted source — the same softness is inherited here and disclosed). The model lands below the band (see MILESTONE-18.md for the measured value and the mechanism); the miss is carried openly, not tuned away.

S6 (Class II pulse >100 vs Class I <100); S7 (Class II 100-120). Direction only — ATLS magnitudes are contested (S7/Mutschler caveat). MILESTONE 18 MAGNITUDE GATE: post-haemorrhage heart rate inside the ATLS Class II band 100-120 /min (S16, Table 2, re-read in-session). 750 mL is the Class I/II boundary volume, so the band's lower edge is the boundary-consistent value. Mutschler caveat (S7/S16) attached: the gate is reported as an ATLS-band check, not as a claim that ATLS bands are precise physiology.

S2 ('as blood volume decreases, pressure and flow decrease' — flow = cardiac output in the systemic circuit).

perturbation_cases.description: Acute hemorrhage of 1,500 mL, removed from the systemic venous compartment at a constant 25.0 mL/s over 60 s (same lumped removal site and protocol as hemorrhage_750). 1,500 mL is the ATLS Class II/III boundary for a 70-kg adult (S16): Class III spans 1,500-2,000 mL (30-40% of blood volume). Expectations are magnitude-gated on heart rate against the Class III band and directional elsewhere (S16 gives no numeric pressure bands: systolic pressure 'Decreased', pulse pressure 'Decreased'). Mutschler caveat (S7/S16) attached to the heart-rate band. Milestone 18 measured outcome (disclosed in MILESTONE-18.md): the model decompensates at this volume — its compensation ceiling — so the Class III heart-rate band is carried as a soft (reported, not gated) line; the directional expectations are the hard gates.

expectations.source: S2 (volume-pressure relation); S16 Class III blood pressure 'Decreased'. No ATLS MAP band exists; magnitude reported, not gated.

S16 (ATLS Class III pulse rate 120-140 /min, Table 2). MAGNITUDE GATE. 1,500 mL is the Class II/III boundary volume, so the band's lower edge is boundary-consistent. SOFT LINE (Milestone 18): reported, not gated. Measured model behaviour at -1,500 mL is decompensation, not the Class III presentation: recruitment capacity (630 mL, S13) plus in-window refill covers under half the loss, no contractility effector exists in the model, and the heart rate saturates its placeholder multiplier bound (144/min at the 2.4 bound) with MAP in the mid-20s. Gating this line would gate a state the patient in the source table is not in; the miss and its mechanism are reported in MILESTONE-18.md instead. MILESTONE 21 AMENDMENT: the contractility effector whose absence this line records now exists (S13 elastance effector; contractility_* parameters). Measured behaviour with it: the -1,500 mL picture is essentially unmoved (post MAP 29.1 -> 29.6 mmHg; heart rate still saturates its placeholder bound at 144.0 /min; post stroke volume ~7.6 mL) — at this loss the ventricles are preload-starved, so the cited +/-20% elastance swing multiplies a near-empty chamber. The binding omission is no longer contractility; it is stressed volume / venous return beyond the cited 630 mL recruitment plus in-window refill. The line stays SOFT and the miss is carried in MILESTONE-21.md. MILESTONE 24 RESOLUTION: the venous-return formulation is now computed first-class (MSFP/MCFP/stressed volume/RVR reported for every case; resting MSFP 6.29 mmHg against the cited ~7, S17/S18; resting empirical-vs-formula RVR agreement 6.1%), and the long-horizon course case (hemorrhage_1500_course) measures what this line's window actually samples: the standard post window (30-60 s after the bleed ends) catches the transient nadir of a 60-second bleed. Untreated, the model then recovers on the cited mechanisms alone — recruitment completing over its cited 60 s time constant, refill accumulating: MAP 29.6 -> 68.2 mmHg and heart rate 144.0 -> 108.2 /min by +30 min (the +30 min heart rate inside the Class II band on the effective-deficit reading disclosed in the course case), and 60-minute refill 858.9 mL inside S15's 500-1,000 mL envelope. The ATLS classes are stated for patients under assessment and treatment (S20); no ATLS class describes an untreated patient 60 seconds after a 60-second bleed. The line stays SOFT: its statement is timescale-dependent, and the dependence is now measured and reported in MILESTONE-24.md rather than carried as an unexplained miss.

perturbation_cases.description: Milestone 24 long-horizon course of the 1,500 mL haemorrhage (NOT the standard case protocol): settle/baseline/engage exactly as the standard cases, bleed 1,500 mL over 60 s, then 60 minutes of course sampled at +1/+2/+5/+10/+20/+30/+60 min after the bleed ends, in two arms — untreated, and treated with the ATLS initial fluid bolus (1,000 mL crystalloid over 60 s beginning at the bleed end, S20; in-model the bolus is volume-identical to the infusion_1000 case's fluid and stays intravascular except for the lumped transcapillary escape — real crystalloid redistributes mostly interstitial within the hour, which this engine does not represent; disclosed in MILESTONE-24.md). MILESTONE 25 AMENDMENT: the two omissions that sentence records are now closed. The interstitium is a finite reservoir with a pressure (interstitial_volume_ml, interstitial_compliance_ml_mmhg), so the bolus redistributes on the Starling pathway's time course, and the lumped renal function curve (S23) with constant intake (S23/S24) runs in both arms, so volume is actually excreted over the course. The treated arm's retention of the bolus at +60 min is now measured against S27's post-distribution figure (bolus_retention_60min, soft line below), and both arms' urine output and interstitial volume are reported per sample. The pre-amendment comparison values stand in MILESTONE-24.md. Evaluated by the dedicated evaluator in cases.rs against the expectations below. Rationale: the standard protocol's post window (30-60 s after the bleed ends) samples the transient nadir of a 60-second bleed — before the cited venomotor time constant (60 s, S13) completes even one time constant — while the ATLS classes (S16) and the textbook haemorrhage course (S19) are stated on presentation timescales. This case tests the course, not the nadir.

expectations.source: S19 (Boron & Boulpaep, Response to Hemorrhage): 'After its abrupt initial fall, arterial pressure tends to return to normal' under favourable circumstances, by the two lines of defence (reflex restoration of output/resistance, then capillary exchange restoring volume). Evaluated as untreated MAP at +30 min above untreated MAP at +2 min (the standard window's timescale). Directional hard gate; the recovered magnitude is reported, not gated — the same source notes pressure falls irreversibly in some cases, so the gate tests which branch this model is on, and MILESTONE-24.md reports the branch with its mechanism.

S2 ('as blood volume increases, pressure and flow increase') applied comparatively: at +10 min after the bleed ends, the arm given the ATLS 1 L bolus (S20) must sit above the untreated arm's MAP at the same minute. Mechanism-level expectation, hard gate.
S2 (volume-flow relation), comparative form as for treated_map_advantage_10min. Hard gate.

S19: tachycardia tracks the severity of the volume deficit ('the degree of tachycardia is an index of the severity of the haemorrhage'); restoring 1,000 of 1,500 mL must therefore relieve heart rate relative to the untreated arm at the same minute. Comparative directional expectation, hard gate.

S15: refill 'can restore plasma volume by 500-1000 mL within 1-2 hours'. SOFT LINE: S15's figure is stated for moderate loss; applying its envelope to a 1,500 mL loss at +60 min is an extrapolation, disclosed here and in MILESTONE-24.md. S19's independent statement (interstitial fluid replaces ~75% of the shed volume within an hour) would put the figure higher still; the model is read against the more conservative envelope and the comparison to both is reported. MILESTONE 26 MEASUREMENT: with the oncotic term in the Starling driver, untreated refill at +60 min reads 436.6 mL — below this envelope, a disclosed soft miss. Mechanism: refill fluid carries the interstitial protein concentration (3 g/dL, S29), so sustained refill dilutes plasma protein (plasma oncotic pressure 27.0 -> 22.5 mmHg over the hour) and the oncotic term brakes the very flow it feeds — refill is self-limiting in a way the Milestone 24/25 pressure-deficit-only driver could not represent. The sweep in MILESTONE-26.md shows the reading is robust: 429-464 mL across the whole cited sigma span (S30) and at the conductance ceiling, and no in-band calibration reaches 500 mL without failing the gated 30-minute refill observation. The line stays SOFT, the band stays as written, and the miss is carried openly.

S16 ATLS Class II pulse band 100-120 /min. SOFT LINE, and an interpretation, stated openly: by +30 min the untreated model's own refill has replaced roughly 40% of the loss, so its effective remaining deficit is of Class II size (~900 mL); reading the +30 min heart rate against the Class II band tests whether the settled untreated picture is class-coherent. It is NOT a claim that a 1,500 mL patient presents as Class II — the nominal class is II/III boundary and the early course (see the +2/+5 min samples in MILESTONE-24.md) is read against Class III. MILESTONE 26 MEASUREMENT: the +30 min heart rate reads 129.6 /min, above the Class II band — a disclosed soft miss, and a direct consequence of the oncotic refill brake recorded on the net_refill line: the effective remaining deficit at +30 min is larger than the Milestone 24/25 engines computed (untreated MAP at +30 min is 66.0 mmHg; Milestone 25 read 68.5), so the Class II effective-deficit reading no longer lands. The line stays SOFT and is read as written.

S16 ATLS Class III pulse band 120-140 /min. SOFT LINE: a Class III patient whose bleeding is controlled and who has received the initial 1 L bolus (S20) but no blood products remains tachycardic in the source presentation. In-model the bolus cannot redistribute interstitially (no interstitial compartment; only the bounded lumped escape), so the model may over-relieve heart rate relative to the band; the reading and that mechanism are reported in MILESTONE-24.md either way. MILESTONE 25 AMENDMENT: the named mechanism is retired — redistribution (finite interstitial reservoir) and renal excretion now act in the treated arm. The line stays SOFT and stays read as written; whether the treated heart rate enters the band under the corrected volume dynamics is measured and reported in MILESTONE-25.md, with no parameter tuned toward it.

S27 (Hahn 2024): 'Following distribution, an infusion is usually found to expand the plasma volume by roughly 20% of the infused volume', rising to ~50% during the infusion — volunteer data. The metric is the treated-minus-untreated blood-volume difference at +60 min as a fraction of the 1,000 mL bolus (the difference construction nets out the arms' shared haemorrhage, recruitment and intake; the arms' urine outputs differ slightly with their different pressures, a second-order term disclosed in MILESTONE-25.md). SOFT LINE: the band's floor is S27's normovolaemic post-distribution retention (0.20) — a hypovolaemic circulation retains MORE, not less (S28: elimination and distribution slow with blood loss), so the floor is conservative for this arm; the ceiling 0.95 is an engineering edge excluding the Milestone 24 artefact (retention ~1.0 because the bolus could not redistribute), not a cited bound. The comparison crosses conditions (volunteers vs a bled model patient), which is why the line is soft. MILESTONE 25 MEASUREMENT NOTE (correcting the ceiling's wording before first use): on THIS difference metric, the Milestone 24 engine's value — derived from MILESTONE-24.md's published refill figures through the volume identity — is 0.37, not ~1.0; the ~1.0 figure describes the bolus's own net Starling persistence in Milestone 24 (the treated arm's net refill stayed positive all hour, so none of the litre ever net-escaped). The ceiling's purpose stands as written: it excludes a treated arm whose blood-volume advantage approaches the whole bolus, which neither engine produces on the difference construction. MILESTONE 26 MEASUREMENT: retention reads 0.08, below the band — a disclosed soft miss. Mechanism: the bolus dilutes plasma oncotic pressure to 14.4 mmHg at +1 min (from 27.0), and through the Milestone 18 conductance the oncotic term drives net escape (net Starling flow -481.8 mL by +60 min); the treated arm's blood-volume advantage over the untreated arm is nearly gone by +60 min (4,024 vs 3,948 mL), though its MAP advantage at +10 min is +7.5 mmHg. Two cautions ride with the number: S27's 0.20 floor is a plasma-expansion fraction in volunteers, while this difference metric additionally nets the untreated arm's own 436.6 mL of refill; and the reading is the most conductance-sensitive output in the Milestone 26 sweep (0.43 at the conductance floor — which fails the gated refill observation — 0.05 at its ceiling; 0.07-0.11 across the sigma span at the shipped conductance). The band stays as written; the miss and its sensitivities are reported in MILESTONE-26.md.

Milestone 26: retention of the whole-blood input at +60 min on the same difference construction as bolus_retention_60min (arm blood-volume advantage over untreated, divided by the 1,026 mL input). Red cells do not cross the capillary wall and plasma protein crosses only at the transcapillary escape the model carries, so retention should sit near 1, against S27's crystalloid post-distribution figure of about 0.20 on the same construction. SOFT LINE: no consulted source states a whole-blood 60-minute retention figure on this metric; the band is an engineering expectation around near-complete retention, disclosed as such. MILESTONE 26 MEASUREMENT: reads 0.66, just below the band's 0.70 floor — a disclosed soft miss on a band that was an engineering expectation, not a cited figure. The mechanism is the metric, not the product: the difference construction nets the untreated arm's own 436.6 mL refill recovery, while the whole-blood arm's own blood volume is flat across the hour (4,610 mL at +2 min, 4,629 mL at +60 min) — the product itself persists essentially completely, as the mechanism states. The components arm reads 0.67 on the same construction, inside its band. The band stays as written.

Milestone 26: retention of the components input (2 units PRBC + 2 units plasma = 1,050 mL, S34/S35 compositions) at +60 min on the same difference construction. Same mechanism and same SOFT status as wb_retention_60min.

Cross-read against S34's rule (one unit raises hematocrit about 3 points in a non-bleeding 70 kg adult at volume equilibrium): the in-course condition differs (post-haemorrhage, refilled, excreting), so the band is a plausibility span around the resting value after 2 units, and the line is SOFT.

Milestone 26: plasma oncotic pressure in the whole-blood arm at +60 min. Whole blood returns protein at the plasma concentration in its plasma fraction, so after the bleed's protein loss the arm should sit below but near S29's resting 28 mmHg; band from that value and the loss arithmetic, disclosed. SOFT (single-model expectation).

Milestone 26: plasma oncotic pressure in the crystalloid arm at +60 min - the dilution endpoint. The arm lost the 1,500 mL bleed's plasma protein and received 1,000 mL of protein-free volume, so its oncotic pressure must sit well below S29's resting 28 mmHg; band from the loss/dilution arithmetic, disclosed. SOFT (single-model expectation).

perturbation_cases.description: Long-horizon refill observation (NOT the standard case protocol): settle and baseline exactly as the standard cases, baroreflex engaged, haemorrhage 750 mL over 60 s, then 30 minutes of undisturbed simulated time after the bleed ends. The reported quantity is the engine's net transcapillary refill state 30 minutes after the bleed ends, as a fraction of the 750 mL lost. Evaluated by the dedicated evaluator in cases.rs against the magnitude range below; the standard window evaluator does not apply to this case.

expectations.source: S15: human volunteer studies — 'about 25% of the lost volume is compensated by fluid recruitment within 30 minutes' after moderate blood loss. 25% of 750 mL = 187.5 mL. The gated band is 15-35% (112.5-262.5 mL): the cited point is S15's; the +/-10-percentage-point width is an engineering tolerance chosen by this project (same disclosure class as the steady-state drift tolerance), NOT a range stated in the source. S14's caution applies: refill after true, necessarily slow blood loss is slower than under rapidly instituted LBNP. The model has no renal excretion, so its refill state is gross interstitial-to-plasma transfer; the cited volunteer figure is net plasma-volume compensation — over 30 minutes the difference is second-order and is disclosed in MILESTONE-18.md. MILESTONE 25 AMENDMENT: renal excretion now exists (the lumped renal function curve, S23), so the refill state remains gross transfer by definition while the PLASMA-side compensation is net of urine; over this 30-minute post-haemorrhage window urine output runs far below baseline (the sensed pressure sits near the curve's zero anchor), so the gross/net difference stays second-order and the gated band is unchanged. The observation now also runs against the interstitial pressure feedback; measured values in MILESTONE-25.md.

perturbation_cases.description: Milestone 30 hormonal arm A (NOT the standard case protocol): settle and baseline exactly as the standard cases, baroreflex engaged; at the moment the reflex engages, 1,000 mL of water is added through the dedicated solute-free water channel over 60 s (an intravenous pure-water load; the crystalloid event channel carries sodium at 140 mmol/L and cannot express it - the channel distinction is measured and recorded in MILESTONE-30.md; the oral route's absorption lag is not modelled), then 4 hours of undisturbed simulated time. A paired no-load control run on the identical protocol supplies the excess-urine difference. Evaluated by the dedicated hormonal evaluator in cases.rs; the standard window evaluator does not apply to this case.

expectations.source: Milestone 30: the osmolality nadir after the load must fall below the constructed resting 286 mOsm/kg (the fall is the mechanism the axis senses) and stay in the physiological band's lower region; the depth depends on the intracellular buffer and the renal response rates, both calibrated constructions. MILESTONE 30 MEASUREMENT: the mark-sampled nadir is 267.6 mOsm/kg AT THE LOAD'S END - the lumped extracellular pool takes the full 1 L dilution before the intracellular buffer equilibrates (by +15 min, with the buffer shared, osmolality reads 273.5, and the whole-body dilution figure is about 279). The band's floor is set below that named lump transient; the post-equilibration values sit inside the physiological band's lower region as the line intends. SOFT (single-model expectation; measured values in MILESTONE-30.md).
S37: AVP follows plasma osmolality along the cited regression - a fall in osmolality must suppress AVP. Evaluated as resting AVP against AVP at +45 min after the load. Directional hard gate.

S39: after ingesting 1 L of water, urine volume rises to about six times normal within 45 minutes. The model's peak interval urine flow over its resting flow is read against a band around that figure. The band is deliberately asymmetric because the protocols differ: S39's load is ORAL (its 45-minute rise includes gastric absorption), while this arm is intravenous and the lumped extracellular pool takes the full dilution at once, so the model's peak runs higher; the ceiling 12 is the AVP-urine-osmolality response curve's own floor ratio at the resting AVP (600/50) - no model carrying these cited anchors can exceed it. MILESTONE 30 MEASUREMENT: peak interval ratio 9.35x (45-60 min interval; instantaneous peak 10.1x at +45 min), inside the band. GATED magnitude line on a cited point, tolerance construction disclosed.

S39: in the same account urine osmolarity falls from 600 to about 100 mOsm/kg as the diuresis peaks. The band [50, 250] runs from S39's dilution floor to a disclosed tolerance above its 100 point. GATED magnitude line.

Milestone 30: cumulative urine at +4 h in the load run minus the paired control run. Most of a 1 L water load should be excreted within hours once AVP is suppressed (S39's account); the band is this project's disclosed expectation, not a cited figure. SOFT (measured values in MILESTONE-30.md).

perturbation_cases.description: Milestone 30 hormonal arm A2 (NOT the standard case protocol): settle and baseline exactly as the standard cases, baroreflex engaged; at engagement, intake (water and sodium together) is set to zero through the intake event, then 12 hours of undisturbed simulated time. The engine carries NO insensible losses, so urine is the only water exit - the arm's osmotic excursion is bounded by that absence, disclosed in MILESTONE-30.md. Evaluated by the dedicated hormonal evaluator in cases.rs.

expectations.source: S37 + S38: rising osmolality (and any pressure deficit) must raise AVP. Evaluated as resting AVP against the hour-12 value. Directional hard gate.

S39: in water deficit, AVP-driven antidiuresis reduces urine volume toward the obligatory minimum set by the solute load. Evaluated as resting flow against the final-hour mean flow. SOFT LINE, and its softness is a measurement record: under the aldosterone limb's first formulation (sodium-CONCENTRATION error signal) the model's final-hour flow read 1.02 mL/min against the resting 1.00 - a soft miss, because sodium excretion stayed up and the solute load floored the flow. With the limb sensing the sodium-CONTENT error (the expansion signal; see aldosterone_sodium_gain), deprivation raises the aldosterone state (to about 2.4x by 12 h), sodium excretion is retained away, the solute load falls, and the flow falls with it: final measurement 0.51 mL/min, a pass. The line stays SOFT because the arm remains bounded by a named absence: the cited physiology describes a body whose water exits include insensible losses (of order 0.5-1 L/day of nearly pure water) and this engine has none, so the arm's osmotic excursion (+1.9 mOsm/kg in 12 h) understates a real deprivation even though every direction is now correct. The missing insensible-loss term is named in MILESTONE-30.md's caveat ledger.
S39: the same antidiuresis concentrates the urine toward the 1,200 mOsm/kg ceiling. Evaluated as resting urine osmolality against the hour-12 readout. Directional hard gate.

Milestone 30 sanity line: with urine as the only exit and AVP concentrating it, 12 h without intake should raise osmolality modestly, not catastrophically; the absent insensible loss (of order 0.5-1 L/day in life) caps the rise in-model. SOFT (single-model expectation; measured values in MILESTONE-30.md).

perturbation_cases.description: Milestone 30 hormonal arm B (NOT the standard case protocol): settle and baseline exactly as the standard cases, baroreflex engaged; at engagement, sodium intake is raised fivefold through the intake event (0.555 mmol/min = 800 mmol/day) with water intake raised threefold in parallel (3.0 mL/min), then 24 hours of undisturbed simulated time. This is the RAAS/aldosterone regime: suppression of the axis must restore sodium balance on the slow (hours) timescale at a small pressure cost. The parallel water rise follows the cited protocol (S44's salt-loading experiments raised salt and water intake together, water freely available) and is measured, not cosmetic: with water intake held at baseline, the same 5x load drives the model onto a hypernatraemic branch ([Na+] 147 mmol/L, osmolality 304 mOsm/kg, ADH 8.0 pg/mL, balance ratio 0.66 at 24 h) because the engine has no thirst - the fixed-water run is the thirst caveat demonstrated, recorded in MILESTONE-30.md. The 24 h horizon is likewise measured: at 12 h the arm had reached only about 60 percent of sodium balance (the coupled water/sodium re-equilibration is slower than the aldosterone limb itself). Evaluated by the dedicated hormonal evaluator in cases.rs.

expectations.source: S43 + S40: raised sodium intake suppresses the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone axis (and reduced intake raises it, S40). Evaluated as the resting aldosterone state (1.0) against the hour-24 value. Directional hard gate.

S45's balance principle (at the new steady state, excretion matches intake) reached through S43's mechanism (axis suppression amplifies pressure natriuresis). Evaluated as the ratio of the final-hour mean sodium excretion to the raised intake; the band is an engineering tolerance around 1.0, disclosed. GATED magnitude line.

S44: sustained about-sixfold salt and water intake in dogs raised MAP only about 6 mmHg with the axis intact. Cross-species, and this arm raises sodium without extra water - the band [0, 15] mmHg is a soft plausibility line around that regime, not a cited human range. SOFT.

Milestone 30: cumulative sodium retained at 24 h (sodium state above its engagement value). It must be positive (part of the load is retained while the new balance establishes) and cannot exceed the 640 mmol delivered above baseline intake over the arm. SOFT bookkeeping line.

sources.locator: MCFP is the pressure in the vasculature when there is no flow, determined by the stressed volume (the volume distending the elastic structures) and the sum of their compliances; Guyton measured it by arresting the circulation and rapidly equilibrating arterial and venous pressures. Cardiac output is determined by the intersection of the cardiac function curve with the venous return curve, VR = (MCFP - Pra) / RVR; at zero flow Pra equals MCFP. The review records that subsequently reported measurements in humans support Guyton's theoretical and animal values.

sources.locator: Mean circulatory pressure (PMC) measured by Guyton's method (fibrillate the heart, rapidly transfer blood aorta-to-vena-cava until pressures equilibrate) at blood volumes varied 0 to +/-30%. A 17 mL/kg haemorrhage was required to bring PMC from 10.7 to 4 mmHg with reflexes intact (0.5 min), vs only 8 mL/kg under blockade (7.8 -> 4) — reflex venoconstriction roughly doubles the loss needed for the same filling-pressure fall, an active compensation of ~9 mL/kg (~630 mL at 70 kg). 'Less than half of the compensation for hemorrhage during the first 5 minutes came from the reflex venoconstriction' — the remainder from passive viscoelastic creep and fluid shifts. Effective total vascular compliance 2.60 mL/kg/mmHg at 0.5 min after a volume change (rising to 4.17 by 5 min).

'It is concluded that the splanchnic bed mobilizes or pools up to 65% of the volume of blood removed from or infused into the cats' — the capacitance compensation this engine lumps into its single systemic venous compartment and venomotor state is, in the experimental record, predominantly splanchnic.

sources.citation: Guyton AC, Hall JE. Textbook of Medical Physiology — Chapter 19, 'Role of the Kidneys in Long-Term Control of Arterial Pressure and in Hypertension: The Integrated System for Arterial Pressure Regulation' (the renal-body fluid system).
sources.locator: Figure 19-1 (renal urinary output curve, perfused isolated kidney): urine output 'is essentially zero at an arterial pressure of 50 mm Hg, rises to normal at 100 mm Hg, and then to about six to eight times normal at an arterial pressure of 200 mm Hg'; 'an increase in arterial pressure in the human of only a few millimeters of mercury can double renal output of water' (pressure diuresis) and of salt (pressure natriuresis). Figure 19-3 analysis: 'at an arterial pressure of 150 mm Hg, renal output of water and salt is about three times as great as the intake'; the equilibrium point — where the renal output curve intersects the salt-and-water intake line — is the only point at which arterial pressure can remain stable; the two determinants of the long-term pressure level are (1) the pressure shift of the renal output curve and (2) the level of water and salt intake. The chronic (in-vivo, long-term) renal output curve is far steeper than the acute curve of Figure 19-1 — 'this great steepness ... means almost infinite gain' — and is steepened partly by mechanisms beyond the direct pressure effect (sympathetic and hormonal axes). Figure 19-2: transfusion of ~400 mL of blood into a dog (arterial pressure +115 mm Hg) raised urine output up to 12-fold and restored pressure to normal within about 1 hour.

sources.citation: Himeno Y, Ikebuchi M, et al. 'Mechanisms underlying the volume regulation of interstitial fluid by capillaries: a simulation study.' Integrative Medicine Research 2016;5(2) (PMC5381436).
sources.locator: Resting interstitial fluid pressure Pisf0 = -3 mmHg (their Tables 1-2, from Guyton's measurements). Their Model 2 implements the experimental (Guyton) interstitial pressure-volume relation as a fitted function of the fractional volume x = Visf/Visf0 (their eq. 9'): the curve is steep in the negative-pressure region and flattens as volume rises. Local slope of the fit at the operating point: d(Pisf)/dx approximately 30 mmHg per unit fractional change (about 20-55 mmHg across x = 0.92-1.0), which scaled to an 11,000 mL interstitium is a whole-body interstitial compliance of roughly 200-370 mL/mmHg. This engine takes a BAND from that fit ([150, 550] mL/mmHg, covering the refill-visited range of the curve) and calibrates a single lumped slope inside it; the source's per-tissue-unit relation is used only through this local-slope scale, and the curve's nonlinearity is NOT reproduced (see the parameter's note).

sources.citation: Hahn RG. 'Crystalloid fluid management From basic physiology to clinical application.' Frontiers in Physiology 2024;15:1439035 (open access).
sources.locator: 'Following distribution, an infusion is usually found to expand the plasma volume by roughly 20% of the infused volume (Moore et al., 1966; Jacob et al., 2012), which increases to approximately 50% for the duration of the infusion.' Infusions of 250-500 mL expand only the central (plasma) space; 500-1000 mL extends into a rapidly exchanging interstitial space; infusions exceeding 1 L at a high rate recruit a remote, slowly equilibrating interstitial space after 700-800 mL has accumulated in the fast space. Volume-kinetic data from 326 volunteer and patient experiments.

sources.citation: Hahn RG. 'Crystalloid fluids.' In: Hahn RG (ed.), Clinical Fluid Therapy in the Perioperative Setting, Cambridge University Press (chapter consulted via an indexed reproduction, status recorded).
sources.locator: 'Distribution from the plasma to the interstitial fluid space requires 25-30 minutes for completion; hence, infused fluid that raises the CO and MAP remains in the plasma during this period' — distribution half-life approximately 8 min. Recalculated population kinetics (10 healthy volunteers, 2 L infusions over 30 min, haemoglobin-dilution method): elimination half-life approximately 60 min for Ringer's solutions and approximately 130 min for isotonic saline. Elimination half-life is prolonged by anaesthesia, pre-operative stress, dehydration and blood loss.

sources.locator: Plasma proteins total 7.3 g/dL (albumin 4.5, globulins 2.5, fibrinogen 0.3 g/dL). Plasma colloid osmotic (oncotic) pressure 28.0 mmHg (albumin 21.8, globulins 6.0, fibrinogen 0.2 mmHg). Interstitial fluid protein averages about 3 g/dL and interstitial oncotic pressure is 8 mmHg. Net filtration across all capillaries is about 2 mL/min for the whole body, of which about 90% is reabsorbed and about 10% returns to the blood through the lymphatics.

sources.citation: Ahlqvist J; Staub NC (reply). 'Plasma protein osmotic pressure equations for humans.' Journal of Applied Physiology 2003;94:1288-1289 (letters; full text read in-session).
sources.locator: Nitta et al.'s corrected Landis-Pappenheimer equation for plasma colloid osmotic pressure, concentrations in g/dL: pi[mmHg] = alb/C x (2.8 C + 0.18 C^2 + 0.012 C^3) + (C - alb)/C x (0.9 C + 0.12 C^2 + 0.004 C^3), where C is total protein and alb the albumin concentration. The exchange records that equation-to-equation spread is of order 10-15%, partly through the albumin fraction. Evaluated at this model's cited points the equation gives 27.0 mmHg at 7.3 g/dL (albumin fraction 4.5/7.3) against S29's 28.0, and 7.9 mmHg at 3.0 g/dL against S29's 8 - the relation is used as cited, and the small anchor offsets are carried openly (see MILESTONE-26.md).
