sources.citation: Boron WF, Boulpaep EL. Medical Physiology, 3rd ed. - chapter 'Control of Water Content (Extracellular Osmolality)' (textbook chapter read in-session via the doctorlib reproduction; carrier status recorded here).
sources.locator: Plasma osmolality in healthy individuals is about 290 mOsm/kg; a rise as small as 1 percent is detectable and raises AVP; the threshold for AVP release is about 280 mOsm/kg and an increase of about 25 mOsm/kg raises AVP to levels producing maximal antidiuresis. AVP half-life 18 min. A fall of 5-10 percent in effective circulating volume is required before AVP release comparable to osmotic stimuli; the volume state also modifies the osmotic relation's slope and threshold. Ingested water distributes across the intracellular and extracellular compartments on osmolality.

sources.citation: Robertson GL, Athar S. The interaction of blood osmolality and blood volume in the regulation of plasma vasopressin in man. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 1976;42(4):613-620 (primary human study; abstract read in-session via PubMed, PMID 1262438).
sources.locator: In recumbent hydropenic subjects plasma AVP was a linear function of plasma osmolality: AVP = 0.35 x (osmolality - 281.0), r = 0.93; upright: AVP = 0.31 x (osmolality - 277.8); during hypertonic saline infusion: AVP = 0.32 x (osmolality - 282). Blood volume modulates the set-point modestly (the relation's intercept/slope shift with posture and volume state).

sources.citation: Kliegman RM et al. (Rudolph's Pediatrics lineage). 'Primary Disturbances in Water Homeostasis' (textbook chapter read in-session via AccessPediatrics / McGraw Hill; carrier status recorded here).
sources.locator: Total blood osmolality normally 280-290 mOsm/kg; osmotic threshold of AVP secretion 283 mOsm/kg, above which AVP rises proportionally to a maximum of about 20 pg/mL at 320 mOsm/kg. A decrease of 8 percent or more in intravascular volume or blood pressure triggers AVP release; at a 25 percent decrease AVP reaches 20-30 times normal (constricting arterioles in that range). Maximal antidiuresis is achieved at an AVP of about 5 pg/mL. AVP plasma half-life 5-10 min.

sources.citation: Guyton AC, Hall JE. Textbook of Medical Physiology - ch. 28, 'Regulation of Extracellular Fluid Osmolarity and Sodium Concentration' (full chapter read in-session via the doctorlib reproduction; carrier status recorded here).
sources.locator: Urine osmolality spans about 50 mOsm/kg (excess water) to 1,200-1,400 (water deficit). After ingesting 1 L of water, urine volume rises to about six times normal within 45 minutes and urine osmolarity falls from 600 to about 100 mOsm/kg, while total solute excretion remains relatively constant - ADH changes water excretion, not solute excretion. The kidney can excrete up to about 20 L/day of dilute urine.

sources.citation: Barrett KE et al. Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 23rd ed. - renal physiology chapters (textbook read in-session via a full-text reproduction; carrier status recorded here).
sources.locator: Mineralocorticoid action has a latent period of 10-30 min before effects on sodium reabsorption manifest, because the action is mediated by protein synthesis. Reduced salt intake raises plasma aldosterone and produces marked but slowly developing decreases in sodium excretion. Water diuresis begins about 15 min after water ingestion and is maximal at about 40 min. Table 38-9: filtered sodium load about 18,125 microEq/min against about 125 microEq/min excreted.

sources.citation: Sonnenblick EH, Cannon PJ, Laragh JH. The nature of the action of intravenous aldosterone: evidence for a latent period and for an effect on urinary sodium excretion. J Clin Invest. 1961 (primary human study; full text read in-session via PMC).
sources.locator: Intravenous aldosterone in man: a latent period of about 20-60 min intervenes before a demonstrable effect on urinary sodium excretion appears (unlike the plasma half-life of 5-15 min); peak effect on urinary sodium at 2-4 h; the action lasted about 6 h.

sources.locator: Aldosterone plasma half-life about 20 min; because increased transport requires synthesis of new proteins (including Na+-K+ ATPase), physiological transport changes begin after about 45 min and peak hours later.
